subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee inline Windows exec support for PowerShell `$...` expansion syntax through the approval path, or document those commands as unsupported/script-file-only?
rationale: The source shows an intentional approval-analysis rejection today, while the open fix changes command-execution approval semantics and needs a maintainer-owned command-fidelity/security decision plus real Windows proof.

options.title: Land Proof-Backed Expansion Support
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322 and merge only after redacted Windows/Gateway proof shows expansion-bearing commands reach one-shot explicit approval without hanging or auto-reviewing.

options.title: Document Script-File Limitation
options.body: If inline PowerShell expansion is intentionally unsupported, update exec docs/tool guidance with the script-file pattern and close this issue as documented behavior after that lands.

options.title: Request Narrower Repro First
options.body: Ask for a current-main Windows proof transcript covering direct exec, nested `powershell -Command`, and `cmd /c` so maintainers can choose the contract from current behavior.

recommendation.title: Land Proof-Backed Expansion Support
recommendation.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322 and merge only after redacted Windows/Gateway proof shows expansion-bearing commands reach one-shot explicit approval without hanging or auto-reviewing.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to the PowerShell-on-Windows switch and Windows exec allowlist flow, making him the best available owner for the command-fidelity decision.
